implementationPlan.description: ARMS FIRST (a roster row without its trio merely MOVES the red — the established fleet finding this task's description pins; the row lands only ALONGSIDE its three arms). For EACH layer add real BEFORE/AFTER/RACE cases to the chosen axis case table, driving PRODUCTION surfaces over real stores — never importing a producer's .test.ts, never reimplementing its authority: (A) FOUNDATION_DISPATCH_DERIVATION_LAYER — recommended axis scheduler-activation (subject: WHICH Foundation node dispatches = admission authority; the roster's subject-wins rule governs, record the decision either way): BEFORE = hostile derivation input before any authority is admitted (e.g. derive for a project whose durable graph is absent/foreign — the caller cannot smuggle a snapshot; assert the exact passthrough code and layer); AFTER = durable authority mutated after derivation (tamper the committed graph body through the store's own write API, re-derive, assert the refusal — sealed-state-no-longer-proving); RACE = two independently hostile concurrent production calls (parallel derivations against conflicting seeded states — assert both refuse with exact code+layer, zero cross-contamination). (B) SAFE_BOUNDARY_OBSERVATION_LAYER — recommended axis durable-store (it derives FROM the durable provider-run record and WRITES a durable observation; runtime-provider is the honest documented alternative — decide by subject-wins and record why): the module's own header specifies the arms — BEFORE on the UNOBSERVED third arm of ClaudeLaunchExit (non-null exit that still proves nothing — the reason a naive `exit !== null` predicate is wrong; assert the REASON code, EXIT_UNOBSERVED family); AFTER on record-present-but-not-proving (durable run record exists but truth/terminal/end fails the predicate — assert TRUTH_INADEQUATE / TERMINAL_UNCLASSIFIED / END_UNRECORDED as measured); RACE on COMMIT_CONFLICT (two concurrent recordSafeBoundaryObservation writers at the same identity — exactly one commits, the loser refuses with the pinned code). Every generated sweep asserts nonzero cardinality BEFORE outcomes; every refusal pins code AND layer literal.
implementationPlan.note:
ARMS FIRST — six arms landed and PASSING before any roster row exists. No producer `.test.ts` imported; no producer authority restated; every arm drives the real module over a real file-backed store.

(A) FOUNDATION_DISPATCH_DERIVATION_LAYER, axis scheduler-activation, new table `tests/security/foundation-dispatch-hostile-cases.ts`. Every arm hands the derivation the two facts the entry used to forward (`graphSnapshot` + `inputManifest`, cast in through a named `hostile<T>()`) and asserts they buy nothing.
- BEFORE `ACTIVE_GRAPH_ABSENT` @ `ACTIVE_GRAPH_PROJECTION` — deliberately NOT this layer's own literal: the refusal travels UNRESTAMPED, and the arm pins which authority answered. Empty durable world.
- AFTER `FOUNDATION_DISPATCH_PROJECT_STATE_ABSENT` @ `DAEMON_FOUNDATION_DISPATCH_DERIVATION` — lawful ACTIVE graph + body seeded, so the projection ADMITS and this code is unreachable in production until `graph.ok` holds; that is the arm's own proof it got past the earlier authority.
- RACE same code+layer, `maxAdmitted: 0`, two connections to one file, sides deliberately ASYMMETRIC (left supplies a catalog that would let derivation continue if the state check were skipped; right supplies one that throws if ever read) so it tests isolation, not dedup. `durableAdmissions` = measured `readEventHorizon` delta = 0.
The lawful ACTIVE graph comes from the planning-graph slice's own seeder (new 6-line export `seedAcceptedActiveGraph`, same content and driver as its accepted control) — re-deriving revision history would police a copy of the reducer.

(B) SAFE_BOUNDARY_OBSERVATION_LAYER, axis durable-store, new module `tests/security/safe-boundary-observation-scenarios.ts`; wired through the existing generator so the durable-store side of `completeness.security.ts` needs no change.
- BEFORE `SAFE_BOUNDARY_INPUT_MALFORMED` — the caller smuggles its own `safeBoundaryObserved: true`. Exact-key admission REFUSES rather than ignores it; nothing is seeded, because reaching the store would already be the defect.
- AFTER `SAFE_BOUNDARY_OBSERVATION_ABSENT` (upstream PROJECT_MISMATCH) — a REAL observation committed through production, then claimed by a rival project. Every earlier layer admits; only the read-side project check can answer. Durable count stays 1: a refused read must not delete what it could not have.
- RACE `SAFE_BOUNDARY_COMMIT_CONFLICT` @ `DAEMON_SAFE_BOUNDARY_OBSERVATION`, exactly one commit, graded by its own runner. Different command ids on purpose — same ids would be an idempotent REPLAY and would report success to both.

DEVIATION, deliberate and recorded. The plan's BEFORE/AFTER for (B) named the REASON codes (EXIT_UNOBSERVED / TRUTH_INADEQUATE / TERMINAL_UNCLASSIFIED / END_UNRECORDED). Those paths return `ok: true` with a recorded `false` — not refusals — and BOTH candidate axes' generic runners require a refusal (durable-store `assertRefusedWith`; runtime-provider's ledger counts any `ok:true` as an ADMISSION and reds `assertAdmittedNothing`). So the trio is refusal-shaped and the reason codes are asserted in a dedicated positive-control block modelled on "the import-shadow read admits what it should": one variant per clause, cardinality pinned BEFORE any outcome is read, and the observed reason set compared BOTH DIRECTIONS against production's frozen `SAFE_BOUNDARY_REASON_CODES` — an unreachable code reds, an undeclared one reds. Plus the TRUE control (a run the host DID see), without which a predicate hard-wired false would satisfy every other assertion in the file.

FINDING, fixed at the shared helper rather than papered over at the case. `assertRefusedWith` read only `layer`/`reasonLayer`; the whole `FoundationAttemptRefused` family names the answering layer `refusedBy`, so those refusals arrived as a harness MISUSE error — from the case's side indistinguishable from a boundary that named no layer at all. `readRefusal` now reads the third spelling, precedence unchanged, so it can only admit shapes that previously threw. Re-shaping the value inside my case table was the alternative and is worse: it would point the assertion at a test-side normaliser instead of at production's own answer.

GOTCHA worth the next agent's time: the provider-run reader binds the ATTEMPT to the INTENT before it reads any run page, so a run record whose slug does not match the activation that seeded it is refused as a binding mismatch and never reaches the predicate. Cost one red; the fixture now separates IDENTITY (slug) from SHAPE (which clause is broken).
